Purist

PYUR-ist · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Purist is a person who insists on strict adherence to traditional rules, methods, or forms of a discipline.

A total purist about pizza, her uncle refuses to eat any pie that isn't made with San Marzano tomatoes and wood-fired dough.

Worked Example

Grammar purists at the newspaper still insist on never ending a sentence with a preposition, even when the alternative sounds stiff and awkward.

Being someone who insists on strict, traditional correctness in a particular field is exactly what purist describes.

How Purist Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

traditionalist

traditionalist: a person who favors established customs or methods

stickler

stickler: a person who insists on a certain quality or type of behavior

Antonyms

innovator

innovator: a person who introduces new methods or ideas

pragmatist

pragmatist: a person who deals with things practically rather than by strict rules

How Strong Is It? — traditionalist → purist → stickler

traditionalist vs. purist

traditionalist vs. purist: As a traditionalist, the tailor still hand-stitches every button rather than using a machine.

stickler vs. purist

stickler vs. purist: Stickler goes further than purist: a purist insists on traditional methods and forms, while a stickler enforces every rule so fiercely he calls a foul over a half-inch violation.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of purist.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — pur-

root — pur-: clean, unmixed (Latin)

suffix — -ist

suffix — -ist: one who practices or believes in (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Purist combines the Latin root pur- ('clean, unmixed') with the suffix -ist ('one who practices or believes in'). A purist, then, is literally someone devoted to keeping something 'pure' -- unmixed with outside influence or shortcuts.

Use the root in a new word: purify

Use the root in a new word: purify: The new filtration system can purify even heavily polluted water within minutes.

Root Check

Word Choice

Calling someone a purist can be a compliment (dedicated, principled) or a mild criticism (rigid, resistant to reasonable change) depending on tone -- context usually makes clear which one is meant.
